posts.name: kreistor
posts.cooked:
I am not trashing Ra. Ra is an offensive deck. I was discussing Defensive combos. Ra has one. Others have more. LftF is still useful on its own, without TtE and NE. But with LftF and NE, Legacy can at least soak all the melee IL dishes out. Ra does nothing until both TtE and FotSG are in play, since IL's normal damage is Melee, not Fire. Legacy can also Heroic Interception to drastically cut down damage, and LftF + Fortitude still reduces IL damage by 2, because Legacy is not Nemesis. With 2 of IL's rings in play (or flipped and 1), Superhuman durability, Fortitude, and LftF reduce damage to 1. Legacy is not as card-locked on damage reduction combos as you pretend... he doesn't need only LftF and NE... he has other options to do the job he was chosen for, which is to soak Villain damage. You can even trick IL when he flips with just NE, if you can burn down Legacy to Lowest HP. Basically, what I am saying is that Ra needs the full combo, but Legacy still gets strong effect if part of the combo is in play.

The deck choices were made for more than just damage dealing. Visionary provided Ongoing destruction, TtE and card drawing for decks that came out weak. Wraith for good damage, Stun Bolt's damage reduction, and Ongoing destruction. Fanatic was in for Ongoing destruction, strong Nemesis effect on Innate and Galvanize, a first Turn EoD if major Ongoing destruction was needed, and a faint hope of Wrathful Retribution for a come-from-behind victory if we fell behind. Turns out there was more opportunity for general damage than expected because Wraith drew two Grappling Hooks (and an Imp weap) at start, then Visionary Enlightened a Mental Divergence in Turn 1. Fanatic did not wind up doing much more than punching IL in the face over and over for 3+3 due to a mediocre start draw. With that, IL fell fast. 32 HP ain't much if the Ongoings are dealt with. Ra could not have replaced any of those. Especially Legacy, pre-draw because one combo is not what Legacy was chosen for. He was selected for Galvanize and IP, suicidal LftF if needed, and all of his damage reduction options which would buy time for tohers to build what they needed. Could we have defeated IL with a straight up overwhelming damage deck build? I will of course try that some day and Ra would definitely be on that team, but I predict grim slaughter. Ra cannot displace Legacy from this team.

When I play as Jim, I tend to just focus fire on the main villain and leave other targets to the other heroes - we normally have enough damage or nerfing abilities (such as Hypersonic Assault) to deal with anything horrible, meanwhile I'm just constantly pew-pewing away doing double-figures of damage at least once a round depending on Bounty and equipment status - Ultimate Target, By Any Means, the Compounded Bow, and of course the wonderful Hat are my primary set-up. The only time I don't go for the Hat ASAP is if there's an environment/ongoing that really has to be destroyed right now, in which case I'll go for a Grenade if there's no-one else around who can deal with it (I think this has only happened once or twice). By the time everything's been dealt with that isn't the main villain, I've usually done most of the work in whittling down their hp. The only game I can think of where I played Jim and didn't really do very much was at the last London meet-up, but that was because of reasons (the nature of that particular game meant that Jim and a few other characters were playing very differently to normal, otherwise it would've been business as usual).

No matter what hero I play as in a game, I feel like it was a good game for me personally if not only did we win, but I made some kind of contribution to the team. It doesn't matter if that's killing off minions, dealing a lot of damage to the main villain, taking out the really horrible ongoings when they come out, sitting there at the highest hp and tanking for everyone, getting other people to take more actions whilst doing very little for myself (this being my primary tactic as the Adept, though even then I sometimes "tank" by way of giving myself so much healing that even if I get hit a few times I'm back up to max hp on my next turn)…even if I only do one thing that seems super-useful such as playing one particular card or using a power that deals with one really horrible thing that would've caused us a lot of trouble if left out, that still counts so I feel like I did a good job :).

Not sure if this is the proper place for this, as it is more luck than combo, but a buddy and I just had a most epic game.

 

Kaagra in the Enclave of the Endlings, heroes were Guise, Scholar, and Chrono-Ranger in that order. He was playing Guise and Scholar, I had CR.

 

It was looking bad, Kaagra ket playing gladiators and we just couldn't muster up good damage. At one point she had all but one of her gladiators and herself on the field.

 

Right before this happened though, we accidentally began an epic set-up. Mindbreaker had come out, and Guise had been hit by 2 people. I had a power usage from ultimate target and asked my friend if he wanted the 1 damage so he'd get mind breaker and we'd get a point. He said sure. Then next turn Guise got Chaos Lord, then the Indiscriminate, then he played Guise the Barbarian.

On the round he played the barbarian he got hit 3 times, once from me, once from the environment, and then once from the villain. Every time he was hit he drew a card (gritty reboot), dealt 4 damage to every target (scholar reduced by 2 from Iron and I regained 1 from the reckless title for a net of 3), then played the bottom card of his deck which generally either allowed him a power usage which he used to heal, or more card plays and draws.

 

The final total was 45 points to 16, and that was all my fault. I miss counted how much damage was coming CR's way and mistimed playing Hunter and Hunted, which ended in both him and guise going down. Luckily Scholar, who'd really only sat and tanked the whole game, was able to drop Kaagra by the 16 hp she had left before they finished us, but it was probably mostly luck (thank you Slamara).

 

Still, we had "The Indiscriminate, Champion Mindbreaker, Chaoslord Guise" and it was worth it... plus CR was "the Reckless Living Weapon", so I guess it was slightly thematic too

World's Greatest Legacy, Fanatic, Tempest

erikoverton:

I think I found the ultimate healing combo:World's Greatest Legacy, Fanatic, Tempest

If you can get all of those cards, it would work, but there are only two Cleansing Downpours in Tempest's deck, two Emboldens, Motivational Charge + Ring in the same game often takes a long time, and the game is typically over before half of those cards hit the table.

That's 7 sustained healing to all hero targets every turn.

Normally, Fanatic cannot trigger others to use powers on her Turn, so not per Turn. On AGL's Turn, it's 3 to everyone and 1 to Tempest. On Fanatic, it's nothing. On Tempest's Turn, it's 4 to everything. That's 7 per Round, not per Turn.

You can make this more reliable with PW Fanatic, which also eliminates the need to find Embolden. If you can get it, great, pop it on Tempest.

Add Argent Adept. Add Captain Cosmic.

  1. AGL MC's, then heals PW Fanatic and passes power to PWF.

  2. PW Fanatic Deals herself 1 damage, plays a card, and passes power to AA.

  3. AGL uses Harp to heal himself 2, uses Lyra to deal 1 damage, uses Drum to Heal 5 targets 1, deals 1 damage. Damage is dealt to 2 Dynamic Syphons on Tempest.

  4. Tempest Heals all 4.

On Fanatic, AGL, and AA turns, all Heroes can trigger others powers, so this combo happens on their Turns. This, though, can be improved. Put one Dynamic Syphon on AA, instead. Now, anytime anyone wants to trigger the Healing circle just hit the Syphon for <4 damage. AA uses the Harp to pass power to AGL, to PWF, back to AA. AA ends with Pipes and 2 Rhapsody of Vigor, and Tempest is Syphon-triggered for one power use. 6 to everyone, and 2 to AA. Every single Hero Turn.

Unlike the other combo cards you mention, AA can often have the cards I mentioned in game. He has wonderful card search and deck Mill capacity to make it happen, where Tempest can find his two CDs at the bottom of the deck and takes longer getting there. Captain Cosmic getting two Dynamic Syphons is not difficult either, if you're playing his base Innate instead of PWCC, and are not facing a lot of Low HP or All Hero damage that wreck Constructs. Truth is, though, you're better off with Team Leader Tachyon than Fanatic, since Tach can more than double rate the necessary combo cards come out in all decks, and trigger the combo with single HP damage. the Combo itself loses a function, but Tachyon gets everything else in play and working much quicker.
